statement: A skew-symmetric (or antisymmetric or antimetric) matrix is a square matrix A whose transpose equals its negative, satisfying A^{\textsf{T}} = -A.

properties.property: Diagonal elements are zero and trace equals zero
properties.why: in a field of characteristic not equal to 2, each diagonal element must be its own additive inverse

properties.property: Vector space dimension of n x n skew-symmetric matrices is (1/2)n(n - 1)
properties.why: the sum and scalar multiples of skew-symmetric matrices are skew-symmetric, and each matrix is determined by the entries strictly above the main diagonal

properties.property: Direct sum decomposition Mat_n = Skew_n ⊕ Sym_n
properties.why: every square matrix over a field of characteristic not 2 uniquely decomposes into (1/2)(A - A^T) + (1/2)(A + A^T) with Skew_n ∩ Sym_n = {0}

properties.property: Inner product characterization: ⟨Ax, y⟩ = -⟨x, Ay⟩ and ⟨x, Ax⟩ = 0 for all x, y in R^n
properties.why: equivalent coordinate-free characterization via the standard real inner product

properties.property: Odd-dimensional skew-symmetric matrices are singular with det(A) = 0
properties.why: det(A) = det(A^T) = det(-A) = (-1)^n det(A) forces det(A) = 0 for odd n in characteristic not 2 (Jacobi's theorem)

properties.property: Even-dimensional determinant is the square of the Pfaffian: det(A) = Pf(A)^2
properties.why: the determinant can be expressed as the square of a polynomial in the matrix entries

properties.property: Eigenvalues of a real skew-symmetric matrix are purely imaginary
properties.why: eigenvalues come in pairs ±λi (with an additional 0 eigenvalue if n is odd)

properties.property: I + A is invertible for real skew-symmetric A
properties.why: eigenvalues are purely imaginary so -1 cannot be an eigenvalue
follows from skew-symmetry and purely imaginary spectrum

properties.property: 3 x 3 cross product representation: a × b = [a]_× b
properties.why: the cross product is bilinear and induces a linear map given by a 3 x 3 skew-symmetric matrix

assumptions.assumption: Entries belong to a field of characteristic not equal to 2 (1 + 1 != 0)
assumptions.breaks_when: the characteristic of the field is 2, where skew-symmetric matrices coincide with symmetric matrices and diagonal elements are not constrained to zero

assumptions.assumption: The matrix A is square (n x n)
assumptions.breaks_when: the matrix is non-square, where the transpose dimension does not match and A^T = -A cannot hold

failure_modes.signature: Skew-symmetric matrices are indistinguishable from symmetric matrices; diagonal entries can be non-zero
failure_modes.cause: In characteristic 2, -1 = 1, reducing the condition A^T = -A to A^T = A
det(A) = (-1)^n det(A) implies det(A) = -det(A) when n is odd, vanishing over fields of characteristic not equal to 2
